title: High-speed camera visualization of the flame acceleration in a tube with and without obstacles
author: Guilherme Lourenço Mejia
abstract: The present work studies the flame acceleration phenomenon inside a closed tube, employing high-speed camera for visualization and pressure transducers for pressure measurements. Four main cases of mixture and tube configuration are considered: H2/Air in smooth tube, H2/Air in tube with obstacles, C3H8/Air in smooth tube, C3H8/Air in tube with obstacles, all using equivalence ratio of 1, initial pressure of 1 bar and room temperature of 293K. Flame propagation mechanisms, deflagration, detonation models and deflagration to detonation transition (DDT) are presented. Numerical calculations are performed for adiabatic isochoric combustion, adiabatic isobaric combustion, and Chapman Jouguet (CJ) detonation characteristics employing thermodynamic codes. Diagrams of (x, t) and (V, x), flame (or shock) position and speed, are determined using camera and pressure data. The flame acceleration is then analyzed and compared to the published results. In the tests without obstacles, the combustion development shows the characteristic tulip flame form. Detonation is achieved for the H2/Air mixture with obstacles, whereas it is not for C3H8/Air with obstacles.
